claims.text: Grain-boundary density controls high-temperature plastic strain in tungsten.
Grain-boundary nature or character controls high-temperature toughness in tungsten.
Tungsten grain boundaries act as active sites for dislocation absorption and emission.
Dislocation absorption and emission at tungsten grain boundaries promote dynamic recovery.
Grain-boundary-mediated dynamic recovery improves tungsten ductility by promoting controlled plastic strain.
Grain-boundary-mediated dynamic recovery improves tungsten toughness.
An optimal fine-grain-size regime exists in which tungsten has enhanced ductility and toughness.
Excessive grain refinement causes grain-boundary sliding to become the dominant deformation mode in tungsten.
Dominant grain-boundary sliding causes premature softening and reduced toughness in fine-grained tungsten.
Conventional tungsten used for plasma-facing components is typically coarse-grained.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing will be used to produce tungsten specimens with systematically varied grain sizes and grain-boundary character distributions.
The temperature interval 800–1200 °C is fusion-relevant for the proposed tungsten plasma-facing-component tests.
Grain-boundary density and character modulate dislocation dynamics during tungsten deformation.
Grain-boundary density and character modulate energy dissipation during cracking in tungsten.
Optimized fine-grained tungsten will exhibit greater high-temperature plastic strain than coarse-grained tungsten.
Optimized fine-grained tungsten will exhibit greater toughness than coarse-grained tungsten.
Systematic grain-size mapping will reveal a threshold below which the beneficial effects diminish and toughness declines.
The grain-size threshold at which dynamic recovery is overtaken by grain-boundary sliding is not known and must be determined experimentally.
Failure to observe a statistically significant improvement in both plastic strain and toughness in fine-grained tungsten relative to the coarse-grained control would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to identify an optimal grain-size threshold before the onset of grain-boundary sliding would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The design proposes changing grain size and grain-boundary character together, so their individual causal effects are confounded despite the stated aim of isolating the hypothesized cause.

The boundary field confines validity to grain sizes above the threshold for dominant grain-boundary sliding, whereas the hypothesis and prediction also assert a specific below-threshold mechanism and toughness decline.
